query: can you cut that down a bit?
answer:
Sure, here's a shorter version. The internet is a global network of networks that all use the same rules, called TCP/IP, to exchange data [1][2]. Data is broken into small packets. Each packet carries a destination IP address, and routers pass it along until it arrives, where the packets are put back together [2]. DNS turns names like wikipedia.org into those IP addresses [3]. Services like the web and email run on top of this network [1].

Sources:
[1] Internet – https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Internet
[2] Internet protocol suite – https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Internet_protocol_suite
[3] Domain Name System – https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Domain_Name_System
